summary: Program missions can await an exact-head pull request with Fractal.awaitPr({ id, repo, pr, head }): the daemon resolves merged and merge-queue-exit outcomes from its existing GitHub observations, without a polling worker turn.

replay.detail: The await-pr host request journals its merged/dequeued outcome or typed AwaitPrFailed under the caller's key. Completed keys replay without registering again; resumed attempts adopt the durable registration and queue-exit baseline.

schema.detail: No client protocol, generated client, table or migration changes. Native wait registration uses internal durable claims.

rules.detail: Waiting does not approve, enqueue or merge a PR and grants no GitHub write authority.

compatibility.detail: New bundles using awaitPr require a daemon and bundled program host that understand await-pr. Update every member eligible to execute those programs before publishing such bundles. Existing program bundles and journaled run/ask results retain their contracts.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon replacement resumes open waits by adopting their existing registration.

manual.detail: Roll compatible daemons before publishing or starting a program that calls awaitPr; no production program is started by this change.

recovery.detail: The current attempt retains its registered PR, requested head and baseline across host or daemon restarts. A moved head resolves as dequeued with reason head-changed; an observed merge queue exit resolves with reason merge-queue-exit, not an inferred GitHub rejection cause.
